answer: A single canyon checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 287 aliases as a result costs 500 bonds held for 16 days each, plus the cedar attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so anyone cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a harbor, before it can post or attest. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
